topics.title: BECE biology marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the functions of the human body systems.
The students should be able to list the major organs in each body system.
The students should be able to draw and label diagrams of the respiratory and circulatory systems.
Introduction:
We have studied different body systems in previous lessons. Today we will revise these systems with focus on BECE questions.
Content:
The human body has several systems working together. The respiratory system helps us breathe using lungs. The circulatory system pumps blood through the body using the heart. The digestive system breaks down food using the stomach and intestines. For example, when you eat pounded yam, the digestive system processes it to give you energy. The nervous system controls body functions using the brain and nerves. Practice drawing diagrams of these systems with clear labels.
Class activity:
Students will work in pairs to draw and label diagrams of three body systems on large paper.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is the main function of the respiratory system?
2. List two organs in the circulatory system.
3. Explain how the digestive system processes food.
4. Which system controls your sense of touch?
Summary:
Today we revised the major body systems and their functions with diagram practice.

topics.title: BECE chemistry marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify common elements in the periodic table.
The students should be able to balance simple chemical equations.
The students should be able to explain types of chemical reactions.
Introduction:
We have learned about elements and compounds in previous lessons. Today we will practice BECE chemistry questions on these topics.
Content:
Elements are pure substances that cannot be broken down further. Common elements include oxygen, hydrogen, carbon and iron. In Nigeria, we use iron to make cooking pots. Compounds are formed when elements combine chemically. For example, water is a compound made of hydrogen and oxygen. Chemical equations show reactions between substances. The equation for burning wood is: Wood + Oxygen → Carbon Dioxide + Water + Heat. We must balance equations by making sure atoms on both sides are equal.
Class activity:
Students will practice balancing five different chemical equations in their notebooks.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name three common elements.
2. What is a compound?
3. Balance this equation: H2 + O2 → H2O
4. Give an example of a chemical reaction in daily life.
Summary:
Today we practiced identifying elements and balancing chemical equations for our BECE exam.

topics.title: BECE physics marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to explain the concept of motion and its types.
The students should be able to solve simple problems on speed and velocity.
The students should be able to differentiate between potential and kinetic energy.
Introduction:
We have studied motion and energy in previous lessons. Today we will practice BECE physics questions on these topics.
Content:
Motion is the change in position of an object. There are different types of motion including linear, circular and oscillatory motion. When a danfo bus moves straight on the road, it shows linear motion. Speed is how fast an object moves. We calculate speed using distance divided by time. Energy is the ability to do work. Potential energy is stored energy like water in a dam. Kinetic energy is energy in motion like a moving car. For example, when you kick a football, it has kinetic energy.
Class activity:
Students will solve five problems calculating speed using distances familiar to them like distance from school to market.
Evaluation questions:
1. Define motion.
2. What is the difference between speed and velocity?
3. Calculate the speed of a car that travels 200km in 4 hours.
4. Give an example of potential energy.
Summary:
Today we practiced solving physics problems on motion and energy for our BECE exam.

topics.title: BECE earth science marathon
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify planets in the solar system.
The students should be able to explain environmental problems in Nigeria.
The students should be able to suggest solutions to environmental degradation.
Introduction:
We have studied space and environment in previous lessons. Today we will practice BECE questions on these topics.
Content:
The solar system consists of the sun and planets that orbit it. The eight planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Earth is our planet and it has life because of its suitable conditions. Environmental problems in Nigeria include deforestation, pollution and desertification. During harmattan season, dust particles cause air pollution. Cutting down trees for firewood leads to soil erosion. We can solve these problems by planting trees, using clean energy and reducing waste.
Class activity:
Students will create posters showing environmental problems in Nigeria and their solutions.
Evaluation questions:
1. Name the planets in the solar system.
2. What is environmental degradation?
3. How does deforestation affect our environment?
4. Suggest two ways to reduce pollution in Nigeria.
Summary:
Today we revised earth science topics focusing on space and environmental issues in Nigeria.

topics.title: Mock examination
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full BECE examination paper.
The students should be able to manage their time effectively during the exam.
The students should be able to show proper examination techniques.
Introduction:
We have been revising different topics in basic science. Today you will practice a full mock examination to prepare for BECE.
Content:
The mock examination will cover all topics in the basic science curriculum. You will have three hours to complete the paper. The paper will have multiple choice questions, theory questions and diagram-drawing questions. Read all instructions carefully before starting. Manage your time by spending more time on questions with higher marks. Check your work before submitting. Remember to write your name and class on the answer sheet.
Class activity:
Students will write a full mock BECE basic science examination under exam conditions.
Evaluation questions:
The mock exam paper itself serves as evaluation with various questions covering all topics.
Summary:
Today you practiced a full examination to build confidence and identify areas needing more revision.

topics.title: Practical revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to perform simple science experiments.
The students should be able to record observations accurately.
The students should be able to draw conclusions from experimental results.
Introduction:
We have learned about experiments in science. Today we will practice some simple experiments to reinforce our understanding.
Content:
In science experiments, we follow specific steps to test ideas. First, state the problem or question. Then form a hypothesis. Next, list materials needed. Then perform the experiment carefully. Record all observations. Finally, draw conclusions. For example, to test if plants need water, we can have two plants - one with water and one without. We observe their growth over a week and record results. Another experiment is testing if objects float or sink in water by placing different items like a stone, wood and plastic bottle in water.
Class activity:
Students will perform two simple experiments: testing the pH of different liquids using litmus paper and separating mixtures using filtration.
Evaluation questions:
1. What are the steps in a scientific experiment?
2. Why is it important to record observations accurately?
3. What conclusion can you draw from testing if plants need water?
4. Name two materials needed for the filtration experiment.
Summary:
Today we practiced performing simple experiments and recording results to improve our practical skills.

topics.title: Weakness clinics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify their weak areas in basic science.
The students should be able to focus revision on identified weaknesses.
The students should be able to explain difficult concepts with examples.
Introduction:
After our mock exam, we know some topics are challenging. Today we will focus on these weak areas to improve our understanding.
Content:
Identifying weak areas is important for effective revision. Common difficult topics in basic science include chemical equations, energy calculations and human systems. For example, many students struggle with balancing equations like 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O. To improve, we practice step by step. First count atoms on each side. Then add coefficients to balance. Another difficult area is energy conversion - like how a kerosene stove converts chemical energy to heat energy. We will focus on these areas with targeted examples and practice questions.
Class activity:
Students will work in groups to create revision cards for topics they find difficult with explanations and examples.
Evaluation questions:
1. What is your weakest topic in basic science?
2. Explain how to balance a chemical equation.
3. Give an example of energy conversion in daily life.
4. How can you improve your understanding of difficult topics?
Summary:
Today we focused on improving our understanding of difficult topics through targeted revision.

topics.title: Speed and accuracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer questions quickly and accurately.
The students should be able to manage time during examinations.
The students should be able to avoid common mistakes in science questions.
Introduction:
For BECE success, we need to answer questions quickly but correctly. Today we will practice speed and accuracy techniques.
Content:
In examinations, time management is crucial. Allocate time based on marks. For example, a 2-mark question should take less time than a 5-mark question. Read questions carefully to avoid mistakes. Underline key words like 'explain' or 'list'. Use shortcuts in calculations. For example, in speed problems, remember speed = distance/time. Practice regularly to improve speed. Common mistakes include misreading questions, incorrect units and careless errors. Check your work before submitting.
Class activity:
Students will complete timed mini-tests with increasing difficulty to build speed and accuracy.
Evaluation questions:
1. How should you allocate time during an exam?
2. What are common mistakes to avoid in science questions?
3. Explain how to improve speed in answering questions.
4. Why is it important to check your work before submitting?
Summary:
Today we practiced techniques to improve speed and accuracy in answering science questions.

topics.title: Final mock
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to complete a full BECE examination under timed conditions.
The students should be able to apply all examination techniques learned.
The students should be able to identify remaining areas of weakness.
Introduction:
We have practiced many aspects of the BECE exam. Today we will do our final mock exam to build confidence.
Content:
The final mock exam simulates the actual BECE examination. You will have three hours to complete the paper covering all topics. Follow proper examination procedures: read instructions carefully, manage time, answer all questions, check your work. The paper will have multiple choice, theory and practical sections. For example, you may need to draw a diagram of the water cycle or balance a chemical equation. Approach the exam calmly and confidently. Use all the techniques we have practiced throughout our revision.
Class activity:
Students will write a full BECE basic science examination under strict exam conditions.
Evaluation questions:
The final mock exam paper serves as evaluation with comprehensive questions covering all topics.
Summary:
Today's final mock exam helped us assess our readiness for the actual BECE examination.

topics.title: BECE readiness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list exam day requirements and tips.
The students should be able to demonstrate proper examination conduct.
The students should be able to prepare mentally for the BECE examination.
Introduction:
Our basic science revision is almost complete. Today we will focus on exam day preparation and readiness for BECE.
Content:
For exam day success, preparation is key. Requirements include your examination slip, pencil, eraser, ruler, sharpener and mathematical set. Arrive early at the exam center, at least 30 minutes before the exam starts. Read all instructions carefully before beginning. Manage your time by starting with questions you know well. For difficult questions, make an educated guess if you're unsure. Stay calm and focused throughout the exam. Remember to eat well before the exam and get enough sleep the night before. For example, eating foods like beans and rice can give you energy for the exam.
Class activity:
Students will role-play examination day scenarios including entering the exam hall and managing time during the exam.
Evaluation questions:
1. What materials should you bring to the exam?
2. How should you manage time during the exam?
3. What should you do if you don't know the answer to a question?
4. Why is it important to stay calm during the exam?
Summary:
Today we prepared thoroughly for the BECE examination with practical tips for exam day success.
